title: project-meta
description: One machine-readable file per repository, holding the facts a human would otherwise have to read the README to learn. Written so a later tool can answer 'what changed in which project this week' without parsing prose. Every field is read from the repository or hand-written and reviewed; nothing here is generated from a guess, and an unknown value is null rather than a plausible-looking string.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the file was written against.

id.description: Repository name, and the stable key across tools.

homepage.description: Live deployment, if one exists. Null means there is none - not that it is unknown.

category.description: One of: game, web-app, mcp-server, developer-tool, security-tool, agent-infrastructure, backend-service, observability, research, template, profile.

platform.description: Where it actually runs, as shipped.

version.description: Declared version, from the package manifest or the newest git tag. Null where the project declares none.

summary.description: The repository's own GitHub description, verbatim.

key_features.description: Claims that hold up if checked against the code.

media.description: Paths relative to the repository root, limited to assets the README actually shows.

tests.description: Null where the project has no suite. A count without a source line does not belong here.

source.description: The line a runner printed, or how the number was composed.

measured.description: ISO date of the run the count came from.

docs.description: Repository-relative filenames, null where the file does not exist.

headline.description: One sentence a post can open with. Describes the project as it is.

primary_link.description: Where a reader should be sent: the live deployment when there is one, the repository otherwise.
